title: 3 Bible-Backed Steps to Calm Anxiety
hook: Anxiety isn’t proof you lack faith. Try these 3 Bible‑backed steps in 90 seconds.
script: Anxiety isn’t proof you lack faith. Try these 3 Bible‑backed steps in 90 seconds. One, Name and Notice. Say, I feel anxious about __. Inhale, The Lord is my shepherd; exhale, I shall not want. Cast it on Him because He cares for you. Two, Pray–Present–Thank. Philippians 4 says bring everything to God. Tell Him what you can’t control, then name one small action you can. Thank Him for being with you right now. Three, Replace Rumination with Rehearsed Truth. Think on whatever is true and praiseworthy. Keep a three‑verse card: Psalm 23:1, Philippians 4:6‑7, Matthew 6:34. Save this for a 60‑second reset. And if anxiety overwhelms, wise counseling is a gift.

title: A 60-Second Bible Meets Brain Reset
hook: If you're feeling anxious, watch this.
script: If you're feeling anxious, watch this. Jesus didn’t shame anxious hearts; He pointed them to the Father’s care in Matthew 6. Here’s a calm, Bible-meets-brain reset. Step 1: Name and Notice. Put a gentle label on the feeling, then slow breath: Inhale, The Lord is my shepherd. Exhale, He leads me. Step 2: Pray–Present–Thank from Philippians 4: Tell God what’s heavy, present your request, thank Him for today’s bread. Write one thing you can’t control and one thing you can. Step 3: Replace Rumination with Truth from Philippians 4:8. Repeat three anchors: God is near, God provides, God guides. Replay this anytime. And reach out to a professional if you need support.

title: Stop Overthinking: Faith’s 60-Second Practice
script: You may be overthinking this. Anxiety loves loops; God offers a path. Try this 60‑second practice. For 15 seconds, Name and Notice: I’m feeling anxious about __. Inhale, The Lord is my shepherd; exhale, I have what I need. Cast it on Him, 1 Peter 5:7. For 30 seconds, Pray–Present–Thank: Father, here’s my request. I release what I can’t control; today I will do __. Thank You for being near. For 15 seconds, Replace Rumination: Speak Philippians 4:8 over your thought and rehearse three verses you carry. Peace grows as you practice. Save this and share it with someone who needs calm. And it’s okay to get counseling—God heals through people, too.
